palette.notes: Code: 23 colours on the still, one ramp with 0 hue shift. Not a pixel-art palette: a low-poly 3D render with grey concrete, brick red and festive red/green accents.

lighting: Flat 3D render light with fluorescent ceiling tubes and a warm interior glow; no hand-placed pixel lighting. Fireworks flash in the night sky.
silhouette: No characters. Props (plastic chairs, panettone, bottles, tree) are blocky low-poly shapes with low-res textures.

motion.timing: Code: median hold 883.3 ms, 0.95 changes/s over 20 s; mostly still shots with a few cuts (around 8.5 s and 15 s on the sheet) and fireworks as the only motion.

texture: Not pixel art: low-poly Blender scene with blurry/pixelated PS1-style textures (liminal-core). Pixelation comes from texture resolution, not drawn pixels.
camera: Static or near-static framed shots; hard cuts between a wide patio, a close table still life and the Christmas tree.

acting.acts: No characters; the empty, lit party room is the subject (liminal mood).
acting.depth: Wide room to close still life to tree corner: depth told by cutting closer, not by characters moving.

techniques: not pixel art: low-poly 3D with low-res textures
empty-room staging for a liminal, nostalgic mood
wide then close then detail cut sequence
one ambient motion (fireworks) over a still scene
feel: not pixel art; empty low-poly party room + held shots + distant fireworks = liminal holiday nostalgia
for_fred: Take the empty-stage idea only: open on the scene with Fred absent for a beat, then let him wander in small at the back. Avoid copying the look; it is 3D, not pixel art.
